intro.title: useLocalStorage
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application that uses the browser's localStorage to persist data across page reloads. You will learn how to create a custom composable function called useLocalStorage to manage state that is automatically saved to and retrieved from localStorage. The main technologies involved are Vue's Composition API, the localStorage web API, and JavaScript's JSON methods for serialization. By the end, you'll understand how to implement a reusable state persistence solution in your Vue projects.
intro.usecase: The useLocalStorage pattern is essential for creating persistent user experiences in real-world Vue applications. You'll see this implemented in dashboard applications that remember user preferences like theme selection or default view settings between sessions. E-commerce sites use it to maintain shopping cart items when users navigate away, while form-heavy applications preserve partially completed data to prevent loss. This pattern also powers features like remembering collapsed/expanded panel states in admin interfaces and maintaining filter selections in data tables across page reloads.
